_about: Screening-level valuation for the ranked companies (Version 2 item 3 + analyst review). Three lenses: listed peers (what the public market pays), deals (what control buyers pay) and a sponsor returns check (the most a buyer could pay and still make its hurdle). Kept separate from the score. Illustrative only, from public data; not a valuation of any company. Skills: valuation-triangulator (lenses and reconciliation), returns-sensitivity (walk-away price, exit flat to entry, debt fixed in pounds).

multiple_ranges._rule: Range applied to latest-year EBITDA. Recurring-type businesses (revenue visibility estimate 0.6 or more) use the services range; project-based businesses use the contractor range. Small EBITDA (under the threshold) takes a size discount.

recurring_services.why: Gamma (UK business communications, 89% recurring revenue) traded near 6x before its bid and was taken private at about 7.6x; Crowe puts listed UK services at 7.5x. Our companies are far smaller, so the range sits at or below these.

project_contractors.why: SPIE, a large listed technical services group, trades near 8x; UK private deals under £250m have a median near 6x. Project-by-project revenue and small size put these at a discount to SPIE.

sponsor_case._rule: Five-year hold, exit at the entry multiple (no multiple expansion), debt sized off EBITDA and held fixed in pounds while the entry price moves, all spare cash repays debt.
sponsor_case._cash: Where a filing has a cash flow statement, capex uses the actual figure and the working-capital drag is 1 minus cash conversion (capped at 30%, never below 0).
